set.body:
Objective:
Build the one resolved runtime schema, expression, and relational-plan algebra shared by DynamicFrame and Scala 3 named-tuple Frame[Schema] APIs, while keeping materialized Table[Schema] values and execution resources outside the logical plan.

Core contracts:
- Stable ColumnId and ExprId are distinct from display names and qualifiers.
- Expr carries value type and nullability evidence; runtime construction validates existential expressions against the same closed operator algebra.
- LogicalPlan is immutable, resolved, valid, and free of live resources, captured closures, backend objects, and invalid column references.
- Frame[Schema] wraps a resolved logical plan; DynamicFrame wraps the same plan plus runtime-only schema evidence; Table[Schema] is materialized data, never a plan node.
- If an ergonomic dynamic builder accumulates errors, it uses a separate PlanDraft or CheckedFrame before resolution.
- Dynamic promotion validates schema compatibility once without copying or executing. Typed erasure preserves the exact runtime schema and logical plan.
- Typed nullable fields use Option[A] or equivalent schema evidence while runtime storage continues to use validity bitmaps.

Canonical first-slice nodes:
Scan, Values by immutable source reference, Project, Filter, Aggregate, Join, Sort, and Limit. Convenience operations including select and withColumn lower to these nodes rather than widening the IR. Union, Distinct, and Window are deferred until the focused local workflow is lawful.

Acceptance:
- Dynamic schema inspection and typed binding share one runtime schema model.
- Named-tuple column-expression scopes provide typed filter, projection, withColumn/alias, grouping, and join construction.
- Match types compute projected, aggregated, renamed, and outer-side-nullable schemas.
- General join conditions expose nested left/right scopes; using-key joins may coalesce only explicit equijoin keys and reject other collisions.
- Compile-negative tests reject missing fields, type-invalid operators, unsafe null use, and ambiguous join references.
- Planning and dynamic binding failures are structured ADTs rather than thrown exceptions across API boundaries.
- JVM and Scala.js produce identical resolved plans for shared fixtures.
